description.summary: the windows that are open, and a way to act on them

protocol.description:
How the ring and the panel know which windows are open and what state each is in, and how they bring one forward, put it away, make it fill the screen or ask it to close. Offered only to programs the compositor trusts with the window list (not to a plugin that was not allowed it).
A window is announced the moment it opens and, from then on, every change to it arrives as a group of events that ends with "done". The program should treat what came since the last "done" as one change. Windows put away (minimised, or hidden by the desktop) stay on the list until they close.

interface.name: trindle_windows_manager_v1

description.summary: where the window list is asked for

interface.description: Binding this is asking for the list. A window object is sent for every window already open, and then one for each that opens later.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The window objects already sent stay usable until they are destroyed.

event.name: window
event.description: Its details follow, ending with "done" on the window.

interface.name: trindle_window_v1
interface.description: Until the compositor sends "gone", requests act on the window it stands for. After "gone" they do nothing.

enum.name: flag
enum.description: The compositor reports all four; a program can ask to change the last three.

entry.name: active
entry.summary: has the keyboard, and is on top

entry.name: maximized
entry.summary: fills the space it is given

request.name: destroy
request.description: Nothing more is sent for it. The window itself is not touched.

request.name: raise
request.description: Takes the desktop to the window's workspace, brings the window back if it was put away, puts it on top and gives it the keyboard.

request.name: close
request.description: The same as pressing its own close button, so it may ask about unsaved work. Asked again after it has had a while to close and has not, the program is ended instead.

request.name: change
request.description: Both are sets of flags. Each flag in turn_on is turned on and each in turn_off is turned off. Asking for a flag to be both on and off, and any flag that cannot be asked for (active), does nothing for that flag. A change the window cannot take (a put-away window cannot be maximised) is ignored.

arg.name: title
arg.summary: the title, as the window set it

description.summary: which program the window belongs to

arg.name: app_id
arg.summary: the program's identifier, empty if it gave none

description.summary: what the window is doing now

event.name: parent

description.summary: the window this one belongs to

event.description: A dialog names the window it opened over. Sent only when it changes, and as null when the window has none.

description.summary: the window is showing on a screen
the window is no longer showing on a screen

event.name: gone
event.description: Nothing more is sent for it. The program should destroy the object.
